pattern_id: Crash-induced vote amnesia enables double-vote and conflicting QCs in same round
description:
In HotStuff-style BFT consensus with a SafetyRules component that persists per-validator voting state (last_voted_round, last_vote), a crash window can cause SafetyData to be rolled back to an earlier round even though a vote for a higher round was already sent. If, after restart, SafetyRules only trusts the persisted SafetyData and does not add any additional protection against double-voting across crashes, a Byzantine leader can equivocate at the same (epoch, round) and obtain two distinct votes from the same honest validator on conflicting blocks. By embedding these two votes into a 3f+1 validator set with f Byzantine validators (including the leader), the adversary can assemble two conflicting Quorum Certificates (QCs) for different blocks at the same round and epoch, violating vote uniqueness and enabling conflicting 3-chains and potentially conflicting commits.

This pattern manifests when:
1. An honest validator H* votes for block L at round r, sending the vote but not yet durably persisting last_voted_round = r / last_vote = Vote(L, r).
2. H* crashes, and on restart its SafetyData reflects only last_voted_round ≤ r-1 and last_vote = None (vote amnesia).
3. A Byzantine leader B0 equivocates and sends a conflicting proposal R also at round r (same parent QC, different block id) to H*.
4. SafetyRules sees round(R) > last_voted_round in storage and, ignoring pre-crash votes, signs Vote(R, r).
5. Using H*’s two votes and up to f other Byzantine/controlled votes, B0 forms two valid QCs QC_L and QC_R for L and R respectively at the same (epoch, round).

A correct implementation must ensure that, even under safety data rollback, an honest validator cannot sign two different votes for the same (epoch, round) on conflicting blocks, and that honest nodes never accept two distinct QCs for the same round and epoch.
trigger_condition: Crash or process kill occurs in the window after an honest validator sends a vote for round r but before SafetyData (last_voted_round, last_vote, locks) is durably persisted; after restart, a Byzantine leader equivocates and sends a conflicting proposal for the same (epoch, round) that passes local QC/lock checks based only on stale persisted state.
test_template:
1. Construct an epoch with a validator set of size 3f+1 and designate one validator H* as the crashable honest node and another B0 as the Byzantine leader.
2. Initialize H*’s SafetyRules with an EpochState and SafetyData that reflect a known parent QC Prev at round r-1 (or earlier), with last_voted_round = r-1 and last_vote = None.
3. Have B0 propose block L at round r extending Prev’s QC and deliver it to H*. Invoke SafetyRules to construct and sign Vote(L, r). Assert that a valid vote is produced and that true SafetyData (if read immediately) would have last_voted_round = r.
4. Simulate a crash window by discarding this updated SafetyData and reinitializing SafetyRules for H* from the original stale SafetyData (last_voted_round = r-1, last_vote = None).
5. After restart, have B0 equivocate and propose a conflicting block R at the same (epoch, round r) with the same parent QC as L but a different block id. Deliver R to H* and invoke SafetyRules to attempt another vote.
6. If SafetyRules returns a second vote Vote(R, r) with a different block id than L, embed both votes into a larger validator set {B0, H_A, H_B, H*} and construct two QCs: QC_L from {H*, H_A, B0} on L and QC_R from {H*, H_B, B0} on R, each with 2f+1 signatures.
7. Verify that both QCs validate under the epoch’s validator verifier, share the same epoch and round, and certify different block ids. Assert that this situation must not be reachable in a correct implementation. If the test observes such a pair of QCs, it indicates the crash-induced vote amnesia double-vote vulnerability.
8. The test should pass (no panic) only if the second vote is rejected or certifies the same block as the first vote, ensuring no conflicting QCs at the same (epoch, round).
